outcome: Brian's subagent routing sends some work to Haiku, sets the reasoning level by tier, applies across sessions, rests on research and first principles, and has a feedback system that improves the rules over time.

asked_by.words: why dont we just update that now across sessions and haiku in some places also and the reaosnign level and we should eawrn the ebst rpactics on this bth form resarch and first rprinciples and set upa feedback ssystme so ti improves over time

entries.criterion: I can see which subagent jobs go to Haiku and that design and review never do.
demonstration: Open the README page
Find the table under 'How it routes' and read the 'easy' row
Read the bullet 'Judging agents never get Haiku'
entries.expected: The easy row names Haiku 5.5 and lists mechanical jobs with a cheap check (renames, searches, log or test-output summaries, running tests, version bumps). The judging-agents bullet lists architect, Plan, reviewer, code-review, project-brain, researcher and anything ending in -reviewer as Sonnet or higher, even under rate-limit pressure.
entries.failure_example: The easy row lists 'design' or 'review', or the judging-agents bullet is missing, or says pressure can push a reviewer to Haiku.

entries.criterion: I can see the reasoning level each tier gets and where each number came from.
demonstration: Open the README page
Read the Effort column of the table under 'How it routes'
Read the paragraph that starts 'Why these defaults'
entries.expected: Easy is low (medium when the prompt is over about 50k tokens), normal is medium at most, hard is high at most, long is unchanged. The paragraph gives a reason for each number and a Source line naming your words on #162 and the research report sections.
entries.failure_example: A number in the table has no reason in the paragraph, or the paragraph has no Source line.

entries.criterion: Every new session of mine starts on Sonnet, not Opus, unless I pick otherwise.
demonstration: Start a new Claude Code session in any folder
Type /model and read which model is current
Open the README page and read the first bullet under 'Limits'
entries.expected: /model shows Sonnet as the current model. The README bullet says a plugin cannot change the main model, that the levers are the settings default (sonnet) and /model or /effort, and gives the 2026-11-05 main-conversation cost.
entries.failure_example: /model shows Opus in a fresh session, or the README says a plugin changes the main model.

entries.criterion: I can see that the rules rest on research and first principles, with the source of each one.
demonstration: Open the research report page
Read section 0, the five-line bottom line
Read section 4, the first-principles cost formula
Go back to the README and check that each rule that was added carries a 'Source:' naming either your words or 'inferred by agent' with the basis
entries.expected: The report states its evidence per claim, marks which claims were read directly and which are inference, and has a first-principles section. Each new rule in the README or code comments has a Source line.
entries.failure_example: A new rule has no Source line, or a claim in the report is not marked direct or inference.

entries.criterion: I can see which tier rules the real outcomes support changing, with the transcripts to read.
demonstration: Open the weekly review sample page
Read the table of agent type, tier, runs, bad runs and cost
Read the decision at the bottom: its evidence, its status and the transcripts to read
Read the sentence about a clean week being weak evidence
entries.expected: Every row shows runs and bad runs by agent type and tier. A proposed decision names the change, its evidence, its status 'proposed' and the transcripts to read, and never lowers a judging agent.
entries.failure_example: A decision proposes lowering reviewer or architect to Haiku, or proposes a change with no evidence line, or the page claims a clean week proves a rule is safe.

entries.criterion: I can see how much of my spend is the main conversation, how much of it is Opus, and what Sonnet would have cost.
demonstration: Open the daily report sample page
Read the line that starts 'Main conversations'
Read the 'Spend by model' table and check the Opus main figure matches the line
entries.expected: The line gives main spend ($514.06), the Opus part ($454.05, 88%) and the cost of the same Opus tokens on Sonnet ($227.02). The table's Opus main figure is $454.05.
entries.failure_example: There is no main-conversation line, or its Opus figure differs from the table.

entries.criterion: A planned second review round is not reported as a redo.
demonstration: Open the daily report sample page
Go to the section 'Redos (a stronger model repeated an earlier run)'
Look for 'Cold review round 2'
entries.expected: The summary says 'Redos: 0' and the section lists none; 'Cold review round 2' does not appear.
entries.failure_example: 'Cold review round 2' is listed as a redo of round 1.

entries.criterion: When I or a session accepts a proposed tier change, the rule actually changes and the decision shows who accepted it and why.
demonstration: Open the weekly review page for the first week after the new rules (2026-W46)
Find a decision marked accepted
Open hooks/lib/pricing.ts at the commit the decision names and read the changed tier or effort value
Read the decision's note for who accepted it and which transcripts they read
entries.expected: The accepted decision names the commit that changed the rule, the rule's new value matches the decision, and the note lists the transcripts read before accepting.
entries.failure_example: A decision is marked accepted but the rule in pricing.ts still has its old value, or the note names no transcripts.

entries.criterion: In a new session, a mechanical subagent task runs on Haiku at low effort and a reviewer runs on Sonnet or higher.
demonstration: Start a new Claude Code session with the router loaded
Ask it to run a subagent that searches the repository for a word
Press ctrl+x tab and the agent's number in the pane and read its Why line
Ask it to run a reviewer subagent on a small diff and read that row
entries.expected: The search agent's row shows the easy tier, Haiku 5.5 and 'effort ≤ low'. The reviewer row shows Sonnet or Opus, never Haiku.
entries.failure_example: The search agent runs on Opus, or the reviewer row shows Haiku 5.5.

requirements.quote: eawrn the ebst rpactics on this bth form resarch

mappings.coverage_reason: A3 checks that the main model default persists into new sessions (settings-level config), and A9 checks that subagent tier routing actually works in a freshly started session — together they would fail if the updates were not applied durably across sessions.
mappings.outcome_reason: The OUTCOME says 'applies across sessions', keeping this requirement in substance.

mappings.coverage_reason: A1 fails if Haiku is not named for the easy tier in the routing table, and A9 fails if a mechanical subagent in a live session does not actually run on Haiku.
mappings.outcome_reason: The OUTCOME says 'sends some work to Haiku', keeping this requirement in substance.

mappings.coverage_reason: A2 fails if the Effort column does not show a named level per tier with a stated reason, and A9 fails if the search agent's live row does not show effort ≤ low.
mappings.outcome_reason: The OUTCOME says 'sets the reasoning level by tier', keeping this requirement in substance.

mappings.coverage_reason: A4 fails if the research report does not exist, does not state evidence per claim, or if the README rules do not carry Source lines naming the research.
mappings.outcome_reason: The OUTCOME says 'rests on research', keeping this requirement in substance.

mappings.coverage_reason: A4 specifically requires a first-principles section (section 4, cost formula) in the report and would fail if no such section exists.
mappings.outcome_reason: The OUTCOME says 'rests on...first principles', keeping this requirement in substance.

mappings.coverage_reason: A5 fails if no weekly review page with a proposed-decision table exists, and A8 fails if no mechanism exists to record an acceptance and apply it — together they confirm a feedback system is in place.
mappings.outcome_reason: The OUTCOME says 'has a feedback system', keeping this requirement in substance.

mappings.coverage_reason: A5 checks that proposed decisions are based on real run evidence, and A8 checks that an accepted decision actually changes a rule value in a named commit — the system would fail both if the rules did not improve from feedback.
mappings.outcome_reason: The OUTCOME says 'that improves the rules over time', keeping this requirement in substance.
